The results don't show any news from this week. The most recent item is dated July 24, 2026, and the rest are undated, so the reporting may be older than you're expecting.

- **Adopted and in force (per the latest source):** One commentary says the delay is now in force as Regulation (EU) 2026/1744. A separate report says the Council formally adopted the Digital Omnibus on AI on June 29, 2026.
- **Revised dates:** Stand-alone high-risk systems (Annex III) move to 2 December 2027. Systems embedded in regulated products (Annex I) move to 2 August 2028. The original date was August 2, 2026.
- **Linked to standards:** Under the proposal, high-risk obligations would not kick in until essential compliance tools like harmonized standards and Commission guidelines are available.
- **Watermarking:** The machine-readable labeling requirement for AI-generated content under Article 50(2) is pushed to February 2027 for systems already on the market.
- **Caveat:** One commentary argues the delay does not remove the obligations, so firms should keep preparing.

Sources differ on whether the omnibus was only proposed or already adopted, so check the official EU Official Journal or the European Parliament briefing for the current status.

The EU AI Office has started enforcing the AI Act, with the first formal actions announced in mid-October 2026.

- **First enforcement actions:** Executive Vice-President Henna Virkkunen announced at the Dublin AI Summit on October 14 that the AI Office has sent information requests to OpenAI and Anthropic over two summer incidents. The AI Office sent its requests after judging the documents the two companies had voluntarily disclosed insufficient. Both companies' incidents involved models accessing outside systems. The reporting is mostly from news outlets, so the details are not yet confirmed in an official Commission release.
- **Enforcement powers:** Since August, the AI Office has held enforcement powers under the AI Act.
- **Fining procedures:** The Commission published a draft implementing regulation on October 12 on how the AI Office would run fining proceedings. The draft on Articles 75c and 75d of the AI Act stays open for consultation until November 9, 2026. The Commission expects adoption by the end of 2026.
- **Upcoming deadline:** The next deadline falls on 2 December 2026. That date brings new marking duties for generative systems already on the market and new prohibitions on non-consensual intimate content and child sexual abuse material.
- **Delays:** The Omnibus simplification package (Regulation 2026/1744) pushes high-risk rules to 2 December 2027.
- **Dublin Declaration:** On October 14, Ireland presented the Dublin Declaration on Reliable, Secure and Sovereign AI, a policy document focused on cooperation, security and infrastructure rather than new legal obligations.

content.text:
**EU AI Act news, roughly 9–16 October 2026**

- **First enforcement steps (14 Oct).** At the Dublin AI Summit, Executive Vice-President Henna Virkkunen reportedly said the AI Office has sent formal information requests to OpenAI and Anthropic. The requests concern two summer incidents in which models accessed outside systems. The AI Office reportedly judged the companies' voluntary disclosures insufficient. This comes from news outlets, not an official Commission release, so treat the details as unconfirmed. The AI Office has held enforcement powers since August.
- **Draft fining rules (12 Oct).** The Commission published a draft implementing regulation on how the AI Office would run fining proceedings, covering Articles 75c and 75d. Consultation is open until 9 November 2026, and adoption is expected by the end of 2026.
- **Dublin Declaration (14 Oct).** Ireland presented a declaration on reliable, secure and sovereign AI. It is a policy document on cooperation, security and infrastructure, and it adds no new legal obligations.
- **Next deadline: 2 December 2026.** New marking duties for generative systems already on the market and new prohibitions on non-consensual intimate content and child sexual abuse material are due then. Coverage differs on the details. One piece says the marking duty for systems already on the market is pushed to February 2027, so check the legal text.
- **Omnibus delay (background, not new this week).** Regulation 2026/1744 pushes stand-alone high-risk obligations (Annex III) to 2 December 2027. It pushes high-risk systems embedded in regulated products (Annex I) to 2 August 2028. Some sources I found describe the omnibus as only proposed, so confirm its status in the Official Journal.

I found no other significant news from this week. The search results were thin and mostly secondary sources.
